Agra tours and local sightseeing

Agra tours covering the Taj Mahal, the Mughal forts and the quieter monuments most day trips skip — private guided tours, sightseeing by car and flexible day plans.

Why Agra

Agra is world-famous for one building, and the Taj Mahal deserves it. But the city also holds Agra Fort, Itimad-ud-Daulah, Mehtab Bagh and Akbar's tomb at Sikandra, all within half an hour of each other.

A day is enough for the headlines. Two days lets you see the Taj at sunrise and sunset, and still have an afternoon for the marble inlay workshops.

Questions people ask about Agra

How many days are enough for Agra?
One day covers the main monuments. Two days lets you take them at a relaxed pace and see the Taj at both sunrise and sunset.
Can I visit Agra from Delhi in one day?
Yes, by private car or by train. Both are comfortable and get you back the same evening.
Which railway station should I use?
Agra has several. Check your ticket for the arriving station — we arrange the transfer from whichever one it is.
Is the Taj Mahal closed any day?
Yes, it is closed to visitors on Fridays. We plan around it.
What should I wear?
Comfortable clothes and walking shoes. The monuments involve more walking than people expect.
Where is the best area to stay in Agra?
Near the Taj Mahal East Gate and along Fatehabad Road, where most of the good hotels are and the Taj is only a short drive away. Staying close makes a sunrise visit much easier.
What local food should I try in Agra?
Agra's petha, a translucent sweet made from ash gourd, and the breakfast of bedai with spicy potato curry and hot jalebi. The city is also known for rich Mughlai dishes.
Is Fatehpur Sikri worth visiting from Agra?
Yes. It is about 40 km away, roughly an hour by car, and Akbar's abandoned red sandstone capital is one of the most impressive sites in north India. It also sits on the road to Jaipur, so it is easy to add on the way.
What is Agra famous for shopping?
Marble inlay work in the same style as the Taj Mahal, along with leather goods, rugs and embroidery. Your guide can take you to workshops where you see the craftsmen at work before deciding to buy anything.
